note: The query each page is written for. scripts/check-keywords.py asserts the query's HEAD TERM appears in four places: title, h1, meta description and the opening paragraph, and that no two pages claim the same term. SEEDED 2026-10-06 from each page's own title, for the 47 pages that exist to answer a query, which is why the title slot passes by construction and the OTHER THREE are what the check is really looking at. The hub, utility, state and manuals pages are deliberately absent: they do not target a query, and declaring one would manufacture a failure rather than find one. Review a target before trusting a pass on it, because the seed assumes the title states the subject and that assumption is the thing worth checking. EXTENDED 2026-10-06 to the state, manuals and hub pages, which declare a term of their own because their distinctive word is the PLACE or the SYSTEM rather than the first noun: 'rv repair oregon' would otherwise head on 'repair', a word on all fifty state pages, and the check would pass everywhere and tell nobody anything. 404, about, contact and signin are NOT declared: they do not target a query, and declaring one would manufacture a failure.
